claims.text: Nearly equiatomic FeCoNi has an fcc structure.
Nearly equiatomic FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Nearly equiatomic FeCoNi has low coercivity.
Controlled annealing can induce nanoscale coherent precipitates within an fcc FeCoNi matrix.
An annealing window exists that permits limited diffusion while remaining below the order-disorder transition temperature of the proposed FeCoNi alloy.
Annealing in that window will precipitate a secondary phase.
The annealing treatment can retain the alloy's nearly equiatomic overall composition.
The annealing treatment can produce uniformly distributed nanoscale coherent precipitates while preserving an overall single-phase fcc structure.
The precipitates introduce local strain fields.
The precipitates modify magnetic anisotropy at particle-matrix interfaces.
The coherent precipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning increases coercivity relative to homogeneous FeCoNi.
Annealed FeCoNi containing the intended precipitates will exhibit more than a 20% coercivity increase relative to rapidly cooled homogeneous FeCoNi.
The coercivity increase can occur while high saturation magnetization is maintained.
Rapid cooling produces a homogeneous fcc FeCoNi baseline without the induced nanoscale precipitate structure.
The coercivity enhancement is expected only when the composition remains nearly equiatomic and the fcc phase is preserved.
The cited CoCrFeMnNi alloy undergoes an irreversible pressure-induced fcc-to-hcp polymorphic transition.
In the cited CoCrFeMnNi system, fcc is stable at high temperature whereas hcp is more thermodynamically favorable at lower temperature.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mediator require precipitation of a secondary phase, whereas the conditions require preservation of an overall single-phase fcc structure. A distinct secondary phase would ordinarily make the material multiphase unless the intended precipitates are instead an ordered domain or composition fluctuation within one crystallographic phase, which is not specified.
